trial_court: District Judge at Alipore, Mat. Suit No. 1420 of 2007
case_name: Dr. Deepak Sharma vs Smt. Vineeta Sharma (Nee Dubey)
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2001 but separated soon after. They decided to divorce by mutual consent and filed a joint petition under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The trial court rejected their application for relaxation of the six months restricted period.

legal_principles.principle: The personal presence of parties before the Court on the second occasion is not mandatory.
legal_principles.held: It is rightly pointed out by Mr. Mukherjee, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner (husband) that all proceedings under the said Act shall be regulated, as far as may be, by the Code of Civil Procedure subject to other provisions contained in the said Act and to such Rules as the High Court may make in this behalf.

legal_principles.principle: Affidavit evidence can be used in divorce by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: Such conclusion was arrived at by Their Lordships as Their Lordships were of the opinion that by virtue of Section 40 of the said Act, provision contained Order 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure which provides for proof of fact on affidavit evidence, is attracted as the application of Order 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not excluded either expressly or by necessary implication.

outcome.final_order: The final order was that the parties' application for divorce by mutual consent was allowed.
